# Denylist for the private-content firewall — PUBLIC repository.
#
# The scanning logic lives in a shared composite action; only this data is local.
# That split is deliberate: a denylist is a list of the things it protects, so
# centralising the data would force the union of every repository's list, and the
# union is the disclosure.
#
# This file therefore holds only GENERIC secret-shape and private-network
# patterns. It deliberately omits any pattern that would identify a person, a
# machine or an organisation — such a pattern IS a description of the thing it
# guards, so committing it to a public repository publishes it.
#
# Do NOT add patterns here to "keep it in step" with an internal list. The
# difference is the design, not drift.
#
# ⚠️ THIS FILE IS NOT THE FIREWALL ACTION'S DEFAULT DENYLIST, and this is the
# one repository where that confusion is possible — the action lives here too.
#
# The action ships NO denylist and must never ship one: a bundled fallback
# would make a caller's missing list look like a clean scan, and would force
# the union of every caller's patterns into a public repo. See
# `.github/actions/firewall/action.yml`.
#
# This is arqtos-actions' OWN caller-supplied list, scoped to its OWN audience,
# read only by this repo's `.github/workflows/firewall.yml`. It sits under
# `.github/scripts/` — the callers' convention — precisely so it is never
# mistaken for action data under `.github/actions/`.
#
#   a new secret-shape pattern (a service's token format)  -> belongs here
#   anything naming or describing a person/host/org        -> does NOT
#
# See ./README.md for the exit-code contract; note that a MISSING denylist exits
# 2 and must never read as clean.

\b(192\.168\.|10\.0\.|10\.1\.|172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[0-1])\.)[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\b
ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36,}
gho_[A-Za-z0-9]{36,}
github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{82,}
lin_api_[A-Za-z0-9]{40,}
op://[A-Za-z0-9_-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+

# Added 2026-08-01 (arqtos-cli#1078): secret-MATERIAL shapes the Go strict
# tier was missing — it caught GitHub PATs while missing AWS access keys and
# PEM private key blocks entirely. Credential FORMATS, so they belong in
# every list including the public ones; the audience split is about IDENTITY
# patterns, not credential shapes.
ghu_[A-Za-z0-9]{36,}
ghs_[A-Za-z0-9]{36,}
ghr_[A-Za-z0-9]{36,}
\bAKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}\b
